title: Finite isomorphism scheme for stable pointed curves
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and $S$ a finite-type $k$-scheme. Let $(W,s_1,\ldots,s_n)$ and $(W',s'_1,\ldots,s'_n)$ be stable pointed curves over $S$, with their markings considered as unordered sets. The functor on $S$-schemes sending $T\to S$ to the isomorphisms $W_T\xrightarrow{\sim}W'_T$ that carry the union of marked sections onto the union of marked sections as closed subschemes is represented by a finite unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism] $S$-scheme. If $S$ is normal and integral, every isomorphism of these unordered pointed curves on the generic fibre extends to a unique isomorphism over $S$. The generic isomorphism need not be the identity.

A stable pointed curve over a scheme $T$ means a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one, whose only singularities are ordinary double points, together with finitely many disjoint sections in its relative smooth locus. On the normalization of each irreducible component of every geometric fibre, a component of genus zero has at least three special points and one of genus one has at least one; special points are inverse images of nodes or markings. An ordinary double point has completed geometric local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. The marking may be empty. A genus is computed on the smooth projective normalization of a geometric component. The markings are unordered when isomorphisms are allowed to permute them.

The notions of field, integral scheme, proper morphism, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, projectivity, finite morphism, surjectivity, function field and field extension use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into some finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means that all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes that is finite over a dense open of its target. Group actions may be nonfaithful and may act on the ground field. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions, fibre products and etaleness use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Normalization, completion and power series use [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]; the genus of a smooth projective geometrically integral curve is [def-pc-genus].

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $S$ is Noetherian. For each permutation $\sigma$, apply [lem-sfb-labelled-stable-isom-unramified] to obtain the separated finite-type unramified scheme $J_\sigma$ of isomorphisms with $u s_i=s'_{\sigma(i)}$.

proof.text: For every DVR diagram for $J_\sigma\to S$, its generic point specifies a labelled isomorphism of the two pulled-back families. By [lem-sfb-stable-labelled-isom-trait-extension] it extends uniquely, so the representing bijection gives exactly one lift to $J_\sigma$. The base is locally Noetherian and $J_\sigma$ is of finite type; [lem-sfb-noetherian-dvr-properness] makes it proper. Its unramifiedness gives local quasi-finiteness by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-quasi-finite-at-points], and [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] makes it finite.

proof.text: Let $I=\coprod_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_n}J_\sigma$. An isomorphism carrying the marked union onto the marked union induces an automorphism of $\coprod_{i=1}^nT$. Let $U_{ij}\subseteq T$ be the inverse image of the $j$th summand under the restriction to the $i$th; it is open and closed. The pieces $T_\sigma=\bigcap_i U_{i,\sigma(i)}$ partition $T$, since on each fibre the induced map permutes the marks. On $T_\sigma$ the isomorphism belongs to $J_\sigma$. Conversely these pieces and their labelled isomorphisms glue to exactly one unordered marked isomorphism. Thus $I$ represents the required functor even on disconnected or nonreduced $T$; preserving the marked union means preserving its closed subscheme structure. The pieces commute with pullback, so the bijection is natural. For $n=0$, the one piece is $T$. The finite disjoint union is finite by repeated application of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-coproduct]. In $I\times_S I=\coprod_{\sigma,\tau}(J_\sigma\times_S J_\tau)$, the diagonal is empty on components with $\sigma\ne\tau$ and is the open diagonal of $J_\sigma$ on each matching component. Hence it is open; local finite type is checked on the open summands, proving unramifiedness [def-weil-unramified-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0CYI (lemma-finite-union-finite); de Jong section 3.8, passage to the nonordered set of sections, written out.

proof.text: Suppose $S$ is normal integral and put $K=k(S)$. The prescribed unordered generic isomorphism is a point $a:\operatorname{Spec}K\to I$ over the generic point, by the representing bijection of step 3. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normal-generic-section-extension] to the finite morphism $I\to S$. It gives exactly one section extending $a$. Under that same representing bijection this is exactly one global unordered pointed isomorphism restricting to the prescribed generic one. No identity condition on its generic value is imposed.
